The main takeaway from our work is that

a hierarchical model that iteratively retrieves and attends to large parts of a long document to produce a sequence of queries can outperform models that retrieve and concatenate smaller parts of documents to produce the final query.
hierarchical attention is an effective way to “navigate” through long documents to answer complex multi-hop questions.

a simple hierarchical structure of long documents, combined with a novel iterative attention mechanism, is sufficient for multi-hop QA systems to “navigate” through long documents and answer questions that require multiple steps of reading.
